item.title: South Sudan: the situation
item.description:
Violence persists in South Sudan with armed groups ambushing civilians, killing two people in Jebel Boma County and five in a road ambush in Warrap County. Security forces seized a truckload of alcohol in Mundri West as part of a substance-abuse crackdown, and a Christian woman was killed after refusing a forced marriage to a Muslim man while two pastors were wounded in a separate attack, prompting women in Greater Mundri to demand protection. The governor of Western Equatoria barred personal bodyguards at SPLM congresses and the governor of Jonglei reported efforts to end clashes in Bor, Duk and Twic East, while elections were postponed again to February 2027. Two battle-related deaths were recorded in 2024, according to UCDP.
